context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for suspicious transactions. It processes 3,000 TPS in AWS region eu-west-1 while adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a strict €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway (External System)
* Fraud Analysts (Actors)
* API Gateway with Fail-Open Circuit Breaker (Container)
* Stateless Scoring Service using Rust/Go and embedded ONNX model runtimes (Container)
* Case Management and Audit Service (Container)
* Decoupled Configuration Store for rules and model weights (Container)
* Managed Database / WORM Object Storage for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs (Container)
* Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) for asynchronous isolation (Container)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway invokes API Gateway via HTTPS using versioned OpenAPI contracts.
* API Gateway routes synchronous scoring requests to the Stateless Scoring Service via gRPC/HTTP.
* Stateless Scoring Service reads models and rules from the Decoupled Configuration Store.
* Stateless Scoring Service asynchronously pushes audit events and case data to DLQs and storage via AWS SDK.
* Fraud Analysts access the Case Management service via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
* AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider for managed infrastructure.
* Go or Rust: Compiled languages chosen for low memory footprint and predictable performance.
* ONNX: Embedded model runtime for sub-50ms P99 scoring latency without GPU clusters.
* Terraform: Infrastructure as Code for environment parity and PCI-DSS compliance automation.
* Managed AWS Services (DynamoDB / Aurora Serverless / S3 WORM): Chosen to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team.

## Rationale
The architecture achieves sub-50ms latency and high availability through compiled runtimes, managed AWS services, and a strict synchronous-asynchronous split. It satisfies stringent compliance and budget constraints using serverless cost controls, IaC automation, and immutable audit patterns suited for a three-engineer team.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS before approval and manages suspicious payment reviews for fraud analysts. The system operates on AWS in eu-west-1, adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts (Users)
- Payment Gateway (External System)
- API Gateway / Payment Gateway Integration Container
- Tokenization/Masking Proxy Container
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container
- Case Management Container
- Model & Rule Registry Service Container
- Audit & Compliance Container
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for local caching

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway sends authorization requests to API Gateway using HTTPS/TLS 1.3.
- Tokenization/Masking Proxy scrubs Primary Account Numbers (PAN) before forwarding data, ensuring analysts never see full card numbers (R-05).
- Real-Time Scoring Engine queries Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) and evaluates transactions synchronously via gRPC/REST within <50ms P99 latency (R-04).
- Real-Time Scoring Engine publishes decisions asynchronously to Amazon SQS/SNS.
- Audit & Compliance Container consumes messages from SQS and stores tamper-evident logs in Amazon S3 Object Lock for 7 years (R-06).
- Case Management Container consumes review tasks for Fraud Analysts interacting via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 (R-02).
- Model & Rule Registry Service supplies immutable scoring models and rules to containers for zero-downtime updates (R-03).

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS with Fargate: Managed container orchestration to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team.
- Amazon Aurora & ElastiCache (Redis): Low-latency data storage and in-memory caching to maintain <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
- Amazon SQS / SNS: Asynchronous event-driven messaging to decouple audit logging from synchronous payment paths.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage satisfying 7-year tamper-evident audit requirements.
- OpenAPI / AsyncAPI: Strict versioned contracts ensuring safe zero-downtime deployments.

## Rationale
The decoupled container architecture isolates real-time scoring from audit and case management workloads, ensuring sub-50ms P99 latency under heavy load. Utilizing managed AWS services on ECS Fargate maintains low operational complexity suitable for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance and budget constraints.

Real-Time Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Scoring Engine Container screens payment authorizations for fraud within strict latency SLAs while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance. It evaluates transactions concurrently and publishes decisions asynchronously within budget and operational constraints.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS with Fargate)
- Model & Rule Registry Service Container
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon SQS / SNS
- AWS CloudWatch

## Relationships
- Tokenization/Masking Proxy Container -> Real-Time Scoring Engine Container: Forwards scrubbed transaction data [gRPC / Protocol Buffers]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Queries local cache for fast transaction evaluation [Redis Protocol]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon SQS / SNS: Publishes scoring decisions asynchronously [AWS SDK]
- Model & Rule Registry Service Container -> Real-Time Scoring Engine Container: Supplies immutable scoring models and rules [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Rust or Go: Selected for predictable, low-latency garbage collection and high CPU core utilization via event-loop execution.
- gRPC with Protocol Buffers: Chosen for zero-copy binary serialization and strict schema validation.
- Amazon ECS with Fargate: Enables stateless scale-out within the 25,000 EUR monthly infrastructure budget.
- OpenTelemetry: Provides low-overhead distributed tracing for latency bottleneck isolation.
- AWS CloudWatch: Monitors real-time saturation metrics and container health for autoscaling.

## Rationale
This architecture uses stateless compute containers and in-memory caching to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. It ensures operational simplicity, strict determinism, and robust auditability suitable for a three-person engineering team.
